newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila group says no need to raise oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Manila group says no need to raise oil prices.

text.p: A Philippine business group said on Thursday oil refiners should not raise prices of petroleum products despite the plunge in the value of the peso.
The Multi-Sectoral Task Force on Power, a group of 1,600 member-industries, said in a statement that oil companies still had two months' worth of stocks.
"It is important that the oil companies do not increase prices yet since an oil price hike has a psychological effect on prices of basic commodities," Task Force chairman Raul Concepcion said.
"Other companies are just waiting for the oil firms to raise prices before making their own price increases."
He added that crude prices are expected to soften with Iraq resuming oil exports.
Oil company sources earlier said that a 29 peso to the dollar rate will translate to an average increase of 60 centavos per litre of petroleum product.
None of the three local oil refiners - Petron Corp, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp and Caltex Philippines Inc - have announced a price adjustment.
The peso has fallen close to 12 percent since last week's effective devaluation by the central bank.
